finding.claim: SQL injection via ORDER BY: the `sort` GET parameter is concatenated directly into the query in list_users_sorted() with no allowlist, escaping or parameterization. An attacker can inject SQL such as a CASE/subquery boolean-based expression to read arbitrary data from the SQLite database, including other tables.
finding.sink: $pdo->query("SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY " . $sort) at list.php:6

trace.note: string concatenation into PDO::query; ORDER BY cannot be bound as a parameter, and no validation is applied

finding.guards_checked: No validation, allowlist or cast on $sort in list_users_sorted(). The sibling list_users_safe() (list.php:10-11) uses an allowlist map and is safe. find_user() (list.php:16-17) uses a prepared statement and is safe. Caveat: the only file in the repo is list.php and nothing calls list_users_sorted(), so reachability depends on a caller outside this directory; the function reads $_GET directly, so I treated it as the entry point.

verdict.reason: list.php:5 reads $_GET['sort'] and list.php:6 concatenates it unvalidated into the ORDER BY query, with no allowlist (unlike list_users_safe at list.php:10-11), so an anonymous requester who reaches this function can inject SQL; the caller is not in the repo, but the function itself takes input straight from $_GET.
